title: Symmetric answers at zero
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $W$ be a natural number. Suppose a table of Boolean answers, indexed by machine-state or tape-symbol queries and two natural-number coordinates, satisfies every checker condition for all $t,a,j$ with $t,a<2^W$ and $j\le |x|+1$, using the input bit supplied at position $j$. Then for every tape selector $\tau$, every $t<2^W$, and the second coordinate $0$, the two symbol queries distinguished by the Boolean sign parameter have equal encoded answers: $\mathrm{sv}(\tau,\mathrm{true},t,0)=\mathrm{sv}(\tau,\mathrm{false},t,0)$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-tape machine over Boolean symbols
A Boolean input word and a natural number width W
The answer table satisfies every checker condition for all t,a<2^W and j≤|x|+1, with the supplied input-bit function
The time coordinate t is less than 2^W
The selector τ is either absent or names one of the machine's work tapes
